messages.content: Analyze this sentence.  "Consydre thou myne condicyon; reflecte upon myne fader. Shall I forsake hym, when he is strycken wyth blyndnesse and destytute, to wrastle wyth infirmitie and penurye, when it lyeth wythin my poure to rendre hys latter yeeres fylled wyth comforte and joye?" Each paragraph of your response must end with the same word it started with, separate paragraphs with a newline.

message.content:
Consydre the sentence as a moral plea in archaic English, asking the hearer to weigh the father's blindness, need, and weakness, Consydre
Thou signals the speaker's direct address to conscience, making the appeal feel personal and urgent, Thou
Myne expresses intimate ownership, framing the father as someone whose suffering is personally felt, Myne
Shall poses a rhetorical question whose implied answer is that, having the power to comfort, one should not abandon the father, Shall
